study type: Multi-method analysis integrating multivariable regression, Mendelian randomization, and paternal negative control analyses on large cohort data.
cohort: The study included data from over 400,000 women.
finding: Higher maternal pre-/early-pregnancy BMI was causally associated with 14 out of 20 adverse pregnancy and perinatal outcomes, including increased odds of conditions like gestational hypertension and caesarean section, and lower odds of maternal anaemia and small-for-gestational-age babies.
mod_finding: Higher maternal BMI was associated with higher odds of caesarean section.
